findings.title: Native cleanup can signal a reused process group after reaping its leader
findings.description: The supervisor polls/reaps the child before entering clean_children. clean_children unconditionally sends signals to the numeric historical process group, and its own poll also reaps before later escalation. Successful workspace Git calls explicitly wait/reap then invoke the same cleanup. Once an empty group leader is reaped, Linux can reuse that numeric ID for an unrelated process group; root-mode cleanup can then signal unrelated host processes. Existing group descendants still require termination, so removing group cleanup is not a valid fix.
evidence: .work/v240/full2-native-group-probe2.log: a reaped child (return code 0) reaches killpg(41000, SIGTERM) under a no-signaling mock. This proves the stale-identity code path, not an observed real PID reuse incident.
All supervisor and Git call sites reviewed. Runtime reviewer independently found the analogous unlaunched POSIX native.ts path.
findings.recommendation: Retain leader identity until cleanup, e.g. observe termination without reaping (waitid WNOWAIT) and finish group/descendant cleanup before final wait. Apply consistently to every caller and add Linux tests for natural completion, ignored TERM, escaped descendants and already-exited leaders.

findings.title: Public-to-internal HTTPS migration silently retains HSTS
findings.description: setup_https copies existing metadata including hsts:true. When changing from public TLS to internal TLS and omitting the optional hsts argument, the validation is skipped and the inherited flag renders Strict-Transport-Security for the internal CA. This contradicts the explicit trusted-public-TLS restriction and can make a browser certificate-trust failure non-bypassable. Explicit internal+hsts:true validation also occurs after preparation side effects.
evidence: .work/v240/full2-hsts-probe.py invokes the actual setup path in a temporary Layout, with operating-system/network boundaries substituted; targetTls=internal, retainedHsts=true, emitsHeader=true. It stops before service actions. No production file or real certificate was changed.
findings.recommendation: Resolve and validate the target HSTS policy before preparation; internal mode must not inherit or render enabled HSTS. Add a migration regression starting with public TLS and hsts:true, plus explicit-invalid-option side-effect checks.

findings.title: Main maintenance examples omit required stop confirmation and edge migration
findings.description: The main uninstall and offline-backup command examples omit the new required --confirm-stop flag, so following the documented workflow now fails before backup. The opening upgrade sequence also omits the actual https-refresh-client-identity step. Later addenda contain parts of the new contract but do not correct these entry-point examples; the compatibility-check date is not clearly distinguished from the current changed tool pins.
evidence: Current deploy.cli/operator contracts and tests were cross-checked against the complete README and recovery procedures. No uninstall or service change was executed.
findings.recommendation: Update the original command examples and stated upgrade sequence; keep historical compatibility observations explicitly historical rather than claiming unperformed new platform validation.

findings.title: Linux cleanup tests still treat a historical PID as durable process identity
findings.description: After cleanup/reaping, these checks require /proc/<old pid> to be absent. PID reuse can make correct termination appear to fail; native_shutdown already obtains pidfds and start times but does not use them for its final assertion. This is a validation reliability issue, separate from the production stale-group signal defect.
evidence: Whole fixture bodies and their cleanup phases inspected. No real PID-reuse failure was induced or claimed. Related TypeScript fixtures are covered by the separate runtime reviewer.
findings.recommendation: Assert termination using the acquired pidfd or matching process start identity. For probe subprocesses, capture a stable identity before the termination boundary and preserve descendant cleanup assertions.
